speaker: Doctor
text: How long has the wound on your right lower leg been present, and have you noticed any changes in its appearance or size? Do you have a history of diabetes, peripheral artery disease, or venous insufficiency?

speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the wound have a well-defined border with surrounding skin discoloration, and do you experience pain or itching in the area? I would like to assess the characteristics of the wound and any signs of infection or arterial compromise.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Large wound on the right lower leg. I also have Chronic leg swelling, Family history of similar leg problems.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Venous Duplex Ultrasound
Given the history of DVT and chronic swelling, I suspect post-thrombotic syndrome leading to a venous stasis ulcer.

text: The ultrasound confirms significant venous reflux and obstruction, which strongly supports a diagnosis of venous stasis ulcer secondary to post-thrombotic syndrome. Do you experience significant pain with walking that improves with rest, or does the pain remain constant regardless of activity?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Deep vein thrombosis in the right leg 5 years prior. No other significant medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works as an accountant.

speaker: Doctor
text: The absence of claudication rules out significant arterial disease, confirming this is a venous etiology. I have sufficient evidence to proceed. DIAGNOSIS READY: Venous stasis ulcer secondary to post-thrombotic syndrome
